root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic branches: the jaw or beard-bearing part of the body, and the bark or outer covering of a plant.
root_idea.development: The bodily branch yields terms for the jaw and beard, while the covering branch yields bark, skins, and the action of stripping or peeling. Derived usage also records winding a turban beneath the jaw.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form لِحْيَة rather than the inflected QAC lemma form.

senses.usage_conditions: In the attested Quran occurrence, it appears in the prepositional possessive expression بِلِحْيَتِي, “by my beard.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Jawbone; either the upper or lower jaw, including the part on which the beard grows in a man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also denote a lateral portion of the lower jaw.

other_classical_meanings.definition: By synecdoche, the beard standing for the whole person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage in which a bodily feature represents its bearer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bark or outer covering of a plant; by extension, the pulp or flesh covering a date stone and the skin of a grape.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for the protective or enclosing layer of vegetal materials.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wind part of one's turban under the lower jaw.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction تَلَحَّى بِعِمَامَتِهِ describes arranging the turban beneath the jaw.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To peel or strip flesh from a bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the flesh as the object and the bone as the point from which it is removed.
